status: experimental integration surface; not production promoted
purpose: Allow external agent platforms, gateways, identity systems, runtimes, and services to selectively invoke AXIOM-MESH trust mechanisms without replacing their native protocol, UX, scheduler, identity layer, or application model.
design_rule: Augment weak guarantees at explicit boundaries; do not require platform replacement and do not allow adapter convenience to bypass Mesh authority invariants.

integration_modes.description: External system sends metadata or candidate evidence for analysis, ranking, anomaly detection, or preflight guidance.
External system asks Mesh to validate identity, delegation, currentness, provenance, receipt, or evidence bindings.
External system presents an exact bounded request and asks Mesh for a local allow/deny/step-up decision.
External platform retains orchestration, but consequential effects execute only after a Mesh-verifiable grant/decision is satisfied at the effect boundary.
External platform sends execution receipts, artifacts, approvals, and provenance to a Mesh-compatible evidence layer for later verification and dispute review.

External platform can use Mesh continuity proofs, key-rotation history, backup/recovery attestations, or user-controlled continuity state while preserving stronger proof requirements for privileged restoration.
integration_modes.mesh_authority_effect: none unless separately admitted by recovery policy

external_value_propositions: Add fail-closed authorization without rewriting the external runtime.
Add attenuation-only delegation around systems that support only coarse roles/scopes.
Add purpose, destination, budget, audience/resource, and expiry binding.
Add cross-protocol authority preservation across MCP, A2A, native APIs, and future adapters.
Add causal composition controls for individually valid actions that become unsafe in sequence.
Add portable, independently verifiable receipts and evidence packs.
Add identity-continuity and service-key rotation separation without requiring a single identity standard.
Add optional strong verification while preserving low-friction advisory uses for weaker signals.
Add governed recovery, revocation, and currentness checks around platforms with weak lifecycle semantics.
Add red-team negative-test fixtures that external implementations can run without adopting AXIOM internals.
prohibited_patterns: external platform name or reputation becoming local authority
discovery or identity verification becoming permission
Mesh verification silently overriding external deny/revocation state
token passthrough or credential forwarding without audience/resource binding
requiring full Mesh adoption where a narrow verification or policy service is sufficient
